dashboard.label: MCP Access & Tools
dashboard.description: Who can call MCP tools, which tools are enabled, and which user actually uses what.

panel.title: Users who can call MCP tools (mcp_tool_execute)

search.query: | rest /services/authentication/users | search [ | rest /services/authorization/roles | search capabilities=mcp_tool_execute | rename title as roles | fields roles ] | eval roles=mvjoin(roles,", ") | table title realname roles

div.b: How MCP tool access works here:

ul.li: Tool enablement is global — every tool in the catalog is enabled for all MCP users (Splunk_MCP_Server mcp_tools_enabled KV store).
Per-user access is gated by the mcp_tool_execute capability (granted via role).
Each tool runs with the user's own Splunk RBAC, so the real per-user boundary is the searchable index scope (table below).

panel.title: User × Tool access matrix (✓ = granted · ✗ = denied)

search.query: | inputlookup mcp_tool_catalog | stats values(tool) as tool | appendcols [ | rest /services/authentication/users | search [ | rest /services/authorization/roles | search capabilities=mcp_tool_execute | rename title as roles | fields roles ] | stats values(title) as user ] | where isnotnull(user) | mvexpand user | mvexpand tool | join type=left user tool [ | inputlookup mcp_tool_denied | eval denied="yes" ] | eval cell=if(denied=="yes","✗","✓") | chart limit=0 values(cell) over user by tool
search `mcp_audit_searches` | rex field=_raw "provenance=\"MCP:Splunk_MCP_Server:(?<tool>[^\"]+)\"" | eval tool=coalesce(tool,"(unknown)") | chart count over user by tool

panel.title: Searchable index scope per MCP role

search.query: | rest /services/authorization/roles | search capabilities=mcp_tool_execute | eval searchable_indexes=mvjoin(srchIndexesAllowed,", ") | table title searchable_indexes | sort title

html.div: Community / non-official MCP — access by account (no mcp_tool_execute capability required). The panels above use the official Splunk MCP Server's capability model and stay empty where that app isn't installed. The panels below derive the access model from the connecting account's RBAC and REST-detected tool usage (user-agent match + endpoint inference) — so it works for custom MCP servers / federation gateways too.

search.query: `mcp_rest_clients` | stats count as rest_calls values(client_label) as detected_as values(useragent) as user_agents by user | join type=left user [ | rest /services/authentication/users | eval user=title, roles=mvjoin('roles',", ") | fields user realname roles ] | table user detected_as roles rest_calls user_agents | sort - rest_calls

panel.title: Account × inferred-tool matrix (REST-based — works for any MCP)

search.query: `mcp_rest_clients` | `mcp_rest_tool_infer` | chart limit=0 count over user by inferred_tool
